financing.summary: Lennar is the most land-light of the large builders: at Aug 31, 2026 it owned about 2% of roughly 488,000 homesites and controlled 98% through options with land banks, land sellers and joint ventures. Its main land financier is Millrose Properties, the REIT it spun off in February 2025 and exited as a shareholder in November 2025 (managed by Kennedy Lewis); Millrose had about $5.9B invested under the Lennar Master Program Agreement at Sep 30, 2026 at an 8.5% yield. Lennar's 10-Q says it bought a significant portion of its land from three land banks in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (two at fiscal 2025 year-end); only Millrose is named, and TPG Angelo Gordon's Essential Housing program is the other one documented publicly. Non-refundable option deposits and pre-acquisition costs have grown to $7.2B (from $3.5B at Nov 30, 2024), and Lennar estimates the land banks' total capital outlay on its controlled homesites at about $18.5B, so the pool of Lennar land-bank paper is very large but concentrated in a few providers. Corporate funding is investment-grade and unsecured: a $3.795B revolver (upsized and extended to 2031 in October 2026), a $1.75B term loan due May 2028, and $2.65B of senior notes after a $600M issue in October 2026; net homebuilding debt to capital rose to 12.7% from 2.8% nine months earlier as cash fell to $1.15B and $650M was drawn on the revolver (cash plus undrawn revolver was about $3.6B at Aug 31, 2026 by our arithmetic; the company did not state a liquidity figure).
financing.land_strategy: Land-light / 'asset-light manufacturing' model, in Lennar's words a pure-play, asset-light homebuilder with just-in-time delivery of finished homesites. Since 2019 it has moved land off balance sheet into 'land option platforms' (land banks) and land developer agreements; the June 2026 investor deck calls the shift complete ('land is now administered through third parties'). Controlled share went from 28% (Q4 2018) to 82% (Nov 30, 2024) to 98% (Nov 30, 2025 and Aug 31, 2026). No numeric target is stated beyond maintaining the land-light model; land banks fund horizontal development up to pre-agreed budgets and Millrose limits purchases to land Lennar expects to use within five years.

Years of owned supply is no longer reported. total_controlled here is owned plus controlled.

land_banking.description: Lennar's primary land bank. Under the Master Program Agreement and Master Option Agreement of Feb 7, 2025, Millrose buys and develops land Lennar designates and Lennar holds options with set takedown schedules, paying deposits and monthly option payments. At Sep 30, 2026 Millrose had $5.87B of invested capital under the Lennar agreement at an 8.5% weighted average yield (3.8-year weighted remaining life); in Q3 2026 Lennar took down $620.9M and Millrose redeployed $545.7M into Lennar land and development.
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-10-26)
land_banking.note: Amount is Millrose's invested capital under the Lennar Master Program Agreement, not Lennar's cost. Millrose's whole portfolio was 156,729 homesites in 834 communities and 30 states; the Lennar homesite count is not broken out. Lennar's share of Millrose's capital is falling: pro forma for the Dream Finders / Beazer funding about 42% of Millrose's asset base is outside the Lennar agreement.

land_banking.description: Lennar's own balance-sheet exposure to Millrose: $1.3B of deposits and pre-acquisition costs on real estate under Millrose option contracts at Aug 31, 2026, up from $1.0B at Nov 30, 2025.

land_banking.source_title: Lennar FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-01-28), note: Variable Interest Entities
land_banking.note: The spin-off press release of Feb 7, 2025 gives the land figure as $5.5B; the 10-K figure is used. The ~$1.0B cash figure is from Millrose FY2025 10-K Item 1, not the Lennar VIE note.

land_banking.description: Rausch Coleman land: on Feb 10, 2025 Millrose bought Rausch Coleman's land (about 25,000 homesites, roughly $859M cash net of Lennar-funded option deposits and holdbacks) while Lennar bought the homebuilding operations; Lennar paid Millrose a further $90.4M of option deposits and holds options on the land.
land_banking.note: The $90.4M additional option deposit is from Lennar's FY2025 10-K VIE note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920760/000162828026003870/R17.htm). Millrose has since funded the land side of other builder acquisitions (New Home Co. / Landsea in 2025; Dream Finders / Beazer in 2026).

land_banking.description: Founder's Rights Agreement: gives Lennar an evergreen Capital Priority Right over a set amount of Millrose's capital, the right to match any lower option rate Millrose gives another builder, a consent right over Millrose leverage above 1:1 debt to equity and over pooling Lennar assets as shared collateral, and pause rights. Amended Aug 27, 2026: capital Millrose raises solely to buy completed build-to-rent homes is now excluded from Lennar's priority (alongside the first $2B of debt and equity Millrose raises), and Lennar's consent right over pledging its optioned properties in shared-collateral financings was restated.
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties Form 8-K dated 2026-08-27 (Item 1.01, amendment to Founder's Rights Agreement)
land_banking.note: Amendment terms are from exhibit 10.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000119312526378466/d83131dex101.htm); whether $2B is a changed figure is not clear because the original text was not read. Description of the rights is from Millrose's FY2025 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000201720626000002/ck0002017206-20251231.htm). The same 8-K amended Millrose's management agreement with Kennedy Lewis (investment guidelines and reimbursable expenses).

land_banking.description: Completed-home sale: in Q3 2026 Millrose bought 1,233 completed single-family homes from Lennar across 18 states as a single-family rental pilot, at an aggregate cost basis of about $333M (about $213M of it financed with limited-recourse secured debt).

land_banking.description: Programmatic land bank dating to 2020. A Master Agreement dated Oct 8, 2020 between AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. and Lennar's Essential Housing Financing, LLC (Lennar Corporation joined as parent guarantor) set up the 'SPV-1 Program': the owner buys land Lennar nominates, grants lot options on a fixed takedown schedule, reimburses development costs, and is protected by an option fee and a parent termination fee; owner equity for the program was capped at $1.0B.
land_banking.source_title: Lennar FY2020 Form 10-K, Exhibit 10.12: Master Agreement with AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. (Oct 8, 2020)
land_banking.note: Amount is the equity cap of the first program, not land deployed and not a current balance. The agreement is 2020 vintage; later program sizes and whether Angelo Gordon is one of the three 'Land Banks' in Lennar's fiscal 2026 10-Q are not disclosed. Notices went to AGWIP Asset Management (Scottsdale) and Angelo, Gordon & Co. (New York).

land_banking.description: Reported current terms: Hunterbrook, citing a California county pension fund's (SBCERA) materials, says Lennar posts a 19.9% upfront deposit with Angelo Gordon (treated as first loss, about twice the roughly 10% at Millrose), with a maximum 40-month term, a rigid monthly takedown schedule, and termination rights and fees if Lennar falls behind; a TPG document cited a 15% IRR on the first Lennar land bank.
land_banking.note: Investigative article critical of Lennar's option-fee accounting; Hunterbrook stated its investment affiliate held no related position at publication. Lennar's Mar 30, 2026 'Statement on Land-Light Strategy' says its disclosures were carefully vetted. Treat the terms as reported, not confirmed by Lennar or TPG.

Related-party status per Millrose Q3 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000119312526447297/R17.htm).

competitor_links.relationship: Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, an affiliate of Kennedy Lewis Investment Management, is Millrose's external manager under a Feb 7, 2025 management agreement (fee 1.25% a year of tangible assets; $88.3M for the first nine months of 2026), so Kennedy Lewis people run Lennar's largest land bank day to day. Lennar holds a management succession consent right over the manager.
competitor_links.source_title: Millrose Properties Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2026, note: Related Party Transactions
competitor_links.note: Fee formula and consent right from Millrose's FY2025 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000201720626000002/ck0002017206-20251231.htm). No separate direct Lennar / Kennedy Lewis land-bank program outside Millrose was found in the sources opened.

competitor_links.relationship: Documented outside land banker to Lennar since 2020: the AG Essential Housing program began with a Lennar master agreement in October 2020 ($1.0B equity cap for the first program). Hunterbrook reported in March 2026 that the relationship continues on tighter terms than Millrose (19.9% deposit, maximum 40-month term, fixed monthly takedowns).
competitor_links.note: The 2020 master agreement is a primary source (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920760/000162828021000722/len-20201130x10kxexh1012.htm); the current terms are secondary reporting. Separately, TPG Real Estate bought a majority of Lennar's Quarterra multifamily platform in December 2025.

ma.description: Lennar completed the purchase of the homebuilding operations of Rausch Coleman Homes (Fayetteville, Arkansas), which delivered about 5,300 homes in 2024 at an average price near $230,000. Lennar recorded $312.6M of assets (mainly homes under construction and finished homesites) and $73.0M of liabilities; cash paid net of cash acquired was $254M. Millrose bought the land (about 25,000 homesites, roughly $859M) and Lennar holds options on it.
ma.map_impact: Rausch Coleman (about 5,300 closings) is now inside Lennar's count rather than a separate builder. Adds Lennar markets in Arkansas (Bentonville/Fayetteville, Little Rock, Jonesboro), Oklahoma (Tulsa, Stillwater), Alabama (Birmingham, Tuscaloosa) and Kansas City, and deepens Houston, San Antonio, Oklahoma City, Huntsville and the Florida Gulf Coast. Shows the template: the land banker buys the target's land, the builder buys only operations.
ma.source_title: Lennar Completes Acquisition of Rausch Coleman Homes (2025-02-10)
ma.note: Asset, liability and cash figures from Lennar's FY2025 10-K (Business Transaction note and MD&A); land figures from Millrose's FY2025 10-K. Total price not disclosed.

ma.description: Taxable spin-off of about 80% of Millrose to Lennar stockholders (120,980,401 Class A and 11,819,811 Class B shares); Lennar contributed $5.6B of land (about 87,000 homesites) and $1.0B of cash and kept about 20% non-voting. Millrose listed on the NYSE as MRP, externally managed by Kennedy Lewis.
ma.map_impact: Creates the public land banker that now competes with Domain for other builders' business while holding most of Lennar's former land. Moves Lennar to roughly 98% optioned homesites and makes Millrose's manager (Kennedy Lewis) the counterparty for most Lennar land decisions.
ma.source_title: Lennar Form 8-K dated 2025-02-07 (Items 7.01, 8.01, Millrose spin-off completion)
ma.note: Cash contribution (~$1.0B, incl. $585M of cash deposit liabilities) and the Kennedy Lewis manager are from Millrose FY2025 10-K Item 1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000201720626000002/ck0002017206-20251231.htm); the cited 8-K states only the share counts, ~20% retention and the MRP listing.

ma.description: Split-off exchange offer: Lennar swapped its remaining 33,298,754 Millrose Class A shares for 8,049,594 of its own Class A shares, cutting investments and equity by $1.1B and booking a one-time $156.1M loss.
ma.map_impact: Lennar no longer owns Millrose and is no longer its related party; the relationship is now purely contractual (Master Program Agreement and Founder's Rights Agreement). Millrose is free-standing as it adds other builders.
ma.source_title: Lennar FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-01-28), note: Business Transaction

ma.counterparty: Quarterra Group (majority interest sold to TPG Real Estate)
ma.description: Lennar sold a majority interest in its Quarterra multifamily development subsidiary to TPG Real Estate, which made a $1.0B strategic commitment; Lennar retained a minority stake and legacy JVs were excluded. Announced Jan 6, 2026.
ma.map_impact: Takes most of the multifamily platform out of Lennar and brings TPG in as a capital partner at the platform level; no change to homebuilding divisions or lots. Quarterra CEO Brad Greiwe stays.
ma.source_title: TPG and Lennar Announce Strategic Partnership to Recapitalize Quarterra (2026-01-06)
ma.note: Price and exact ownership split not disclosed. Sale month from Lennar's FY2025 10-K.
